idiom_name: is check with smart cast (sealed interface + exhaustive when as the static counterpart)
implementation_notes: Kotlin's is (and !is) operator tests the runtime type and the compiler smart-casts the value inside the branch that proved it, so test and handle coincide without an explicit cast: `if (x is Flushable) x.flush()`. A class may implement any number of capability interfaces, and when the capability set is closed the language offers the compile-time alternative: a sealed interface with an exhaustive when needs no else branch and no runtime query, because the compiler knows every direct subtype (kotlinlang.org: direct subclasses of a sealed type are known at compile time). What replaces the classic structure is the check-plus-smart-cast pair, with sealed hierarchies for closed sets; a runtime query stays the right tool when implementers are discovered dynamically, since a plugin cannot extend a sealed hierarchy outside its module.
pitfalls: Smart casts need a stable value: a var or a property with a custom getter cannot be smart-cast, so the test and the use may see different objects - capture the value in a local val first.
Type arguments are erased: `x is List<String>` does not compile for a non-reified type parameter, and a raw check only sees the class.
A sealed hierarchy cannot be extended from another module, so it is not a replacement for capability queries at plugin boundaries.
